summary.one_liner: MetaGPT is a multi-agent framework that assigns roles to LLM agents (product manager, architect, project manager, engineer) so they can collaborate on complex tasks such as generating a software project from a one-line requirement.
summary.what_it_does: Takes a one-line requirement and produces user stories, competitive analysis, requirements, data structures, APIs and other project documents, then generates a code repository. It models a software company as a multi-agent system with standard operating procedures (SOPs), expressed in the README as Code = SOP(Team). It can be run from the CLI with a command like `metagpt "Create a 2048 game"`, which writes output to ./workspace. It can also be used as a Python library, via generate_repo or ProjectRepo. A Data Interpreter agent is included for writing and running code, such as data analysis on a dataset with a plot. The README lists use cases including Data Interpreter, Debate, Researcher and Receipt Assistant, and links to tutorials on building custom agents.
use_cases: generate a software project from a one-line requirement
automated document creation like PRDs and API designs
running data analysis with an AI coding agent
how_to_run: Install Python 3.9 or later, below 3.12, and Node.js with pnpm
Edit ~/.metagpt/config2.yaml with your LLM api_type, model, base_url and api_key
Use as a library: from metagpt.software_company import generate_repo; repo = generate_repo("Create a 2048 game")
stack: Azure, Ollama, Groq and other LLM providers via config
notable: Software-company simulation: product manager, architect, project manager and engineer roles with SOP-driven workflow
Generates a full repo from a one-line prompt via CLI or Python API
Data Interpreter agent for writing and running data-analysis code
Configurable LLM backend through a single YAML file
Research background: papers on AFlow, SPO and AOT cited in the README
caveats: Requires Python 3.9 to below 3.12 and Node.js with pnpm installed before use
Needs an LLM API key or a configured LLM endpoint
README describes the software-company schematic as still being implemented
